elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date"

elements.element: Customer may opt out of renewal on 30 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon 30 days' written notice to the other"
"HDI shall notify the Company in writing of each upcoming automatic renewal not less than 60 days prior to the applicable anniversary"

elements.element: Renewal price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%
elements.evidence: "any increase in the fees payable by the Company for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3%"

elements.evidence: "shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3%"

reasons: All four preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: 12-month automatic renewal, a 30-day exit notice available to the Customer (Company), a 60-day Vendor (HDI) reminder, and a renewal fee cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Edits are minimal: a single number substitution ("ninety (90) days" → "30 days'") plus one concise sentence supplying the two absent mechanics (reminder and price cap); no boilerplate, no new exceptions, no clause rewrite.

Untouched terms (Effective Date definition, one-year initial term, Termination Date notice requirement) remain effective; "HDI" and "Company" are defined parties and CPI is a conventional, self-evident reference in this context.

Minor note only (not a deviation): because the notice mechanic is mutual, the shortened 30-day window also lets HDI exit on shorter notice than the original 90 days; if term stability matters commercially, the notice could be made Customer-only, but the preferred position on non-renewal is satisfied as drafted.
